```{r}
pb_ratio_df <- data.frame(
  study_id = names(prevotella_abund),
  log10_PB_ratio = log10((as.numeric(prevotella_abund) + pseudocount) / (as.numeric(bacteroides_abund) + pseudocount))
)
metadata_from_phy$study_id <- as.character(metadata_from_phy$study_id)
pb_ratio_df$study_id <- as.character(pb_ratio_df$study_id)
analysis_df <- inner_join(pb_ratio_df, metadata_from_phy, by = "study_id")


# 2. DEFINE THE "HIGH P/B RATIO" SUBGROUP
# --------------------------------------------------
# First, let's visualize the distribution of the ratio ONLY within the PE group to find a threshold.
ggplot(filter(analysis_df, study_group == "PE"), aes(x = log10_PB_ratio)) + 
  geom_density(fill = "#ff6347", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_rug() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of P/B Ratio in PE Patients", x = "log10(P/B Ratio)") +
  theme_bw()

# Based on the plot, choose a threshold that separates your ~7 high samples.
# I will use 2.5 as a placeholder. YOU SHOULD ADJUST THIS VALUE.
high_ratio_threshold <- 2.5 

# Create a new column to define the subgroups within the PE patients
pe_subgroups_df <- analysis_df %>%
  filter(study_group == "PE") %>%
  mutate(PE_subgroup = case_when(
    log10_PB_ratio >= high_ratio_threshold ~ "PE_High_Ratio",
    TRUE ~ "PE_Normal_Ratio"
  ))


# 3. CLINICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF SUBGROUPS
# --------------------------------------------------
# Compare clinical variables between the 'PE_High_Ratio' and 'PE_Normal_Ratio' groups.

# Example for a continuous variable: Gestational Age
wilcox.test(gestational_age ~ PE_subgroup, data = pe_subgroups_df)
ggplot(pe_subgroups_df, aes(x = PE_subgroup, y = gestational_age, fill = PE_subgroup)) +
  geom_boxplot() + stat_compare_means() + theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Gestational Age by PE Subgroup")

# Example for a categorical variable: Presence of Severe Features
# Note: 'sev_features_PE_Headache_scotomata' should be a factor (Yes/No)
# table() creates a contingency table for Fisher's test
contingency_table <- table(pe_subgroups_df$PE_subgroup, pe_subgroups_df$sev_features_PE_Headache_scotomata)
fisher.test(contingency_table)

# You should repeat this for all your key clinical variables.


# 4. MICROBIOME DIVERSITY CHARACTERIZATION
# --------------------------------------------------
# Is the overall microbiome different between these two PE subgroups?

# A) Alpha Diversity
# Using the pre-calculated alpha diversity metrics (sha, simp, obs) from your metadata.
# There is no need to recalculate them.

# --- Compare Shannon Diversity ---
# Test
wilcox.test(sha ~ PE_subgroup, data = pe_subgroups_df)

# Plot
ggplot(pe_subgroups_df, aes(x = PE_subgroup, y = sha, fill = PE_subgroup)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Shannon Diversity by PE Subgroup", y = "Shannon Diversity ('sha')")


# --- Compare Simpson Diversity ---
# Test
wilcox.test(simp ~ PE_subgroup, data = pe_subgroups_df)

# Plot
ggplot(pe_subgroups_df, aes(x = PE_subgroup, y = simp, fill = PE_subgroup)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Simpson Diversity by PE Subgroup", y = "Simpson Diversity ('simp')")


# --- Compare Observed Richness ---
# Test
wilcox.test(obs ~ PE_subgroup, data = pe_subgroups_df)

# Plot
ggplot(pe_subgroups_df, aes(x = PE_subgroup, y = obs, fill = PE_subgroup)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Observed Richness by PE Subgroup", y = "Observed Features ('obs')")


# B) Beta Diversity (This section remains the same as before)
# ...
# B) Beta Diversity
# Let's see if the overall community structure is different.
# First, filter the phyloseq object to only include PE samples
phy_pe_only <- subset_samples(phy, study_group == "PE")

# Align metadata with the phyloseq object
pe_meta <- data.frame(sample_data(phy_pe_only))
pe_meta$PE_subgroup <- pe_subgroups_df$PE_subgroup[match(rownames(pe_meta), pe_subgroups_df$study_id)]
sample_data(phy_pe_only) <- pe_meta

# Calculate Bray-Curtis distance
dist_bray_pe <- phyloseq::distance(phy_pe_only, method = "bray")

# Run PERMANOVA (adonis2)
adonis2(dist_bray_pe ~ PE_subgroup, data = pe_meta, permutations = 999)

# Visualize with a PCoA plot
pcoa_pe <- ordinate(phy_pe_only, method = "PCoA", distance = dist_bray_pe)
plot_ordination(phy_pe_only, pcoa_pe, color = "PE_subgroup") +
  theme_bw() +
  stat_ellipse() +
  labs(title = "PCoA of PE Subgroups (Bray-Curtis)")
```
# SCRIPT PARA CARACTERIZACIÓN CLÍNICA DE SUBGRUPOS DE PE

```{r}
# SCRIPT PARA CARACTERIZACIÓN CLÍNICA DE SUBGRUPOS DE PE

# 1. SETUP Y PREPARACIÓN DE DATOS (Asegúrate de tener estos objetos)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
library(phyloseq)
library(dplyr)

# Asumimos que 'phy' y 'analysis_df' ya existen en tu entorno.
# Si no, créalos con los pasos de los scripts anteriores.
# Por completitud, aquí está el código para crear pe_subgroups_df:

# --- Definición del umbral (AJUSTA ESTE VALOR BASADO EN TU GRÁFICO DE DENSIDAD) ---
high_ratio_threshold <- 2.5 

pe_subgroups_df <- analysis_df %>%
  filter(study_group == "PE") %>%
  mutate(PE_subgroup = factor(case_when(
    log10_PB_ratio >= high_ratio_threshold ~ "PE_High_Ratio",
    TRUE ~ "PE_Normal_Ratio"
  )))

# 2. DEFINIR LAS VARIABLES A PROBAR
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creamos un vector con los nombres de todas las columnas de metadatos que queremos comparar.
# He seleccionado las más relevantes de tu lista, omitiendo IDs y fechas.
variables_clinicas_a_probar <- c(
  # Demográficas
  "age", "bmi", "race", "ethnicity", 
  # Historial obstétrico
  "gravid", "par", "pre_weight", "gwg", 
  # Diagnósticos y condiciones
  "probiotic", "antibiotics_during_pregnancy", "infection", "diabetes", 
  "sev_features_PE_Blood_pressure", "sev_features_PE_Renal", 
  "sev_features_PE_Liver", "sev_features_PE_HELLP", "sev_features_PE_Pulmonary_edema",
  "sev_features_PE_Headache_scotomata", "sev_features_PE_Thrombocytopenia",
  # Eventos del parto
  "gestational_age", "term_status", "antibiotic_during_labor",
  # Resultados neonatales
  "baby_weight", "sex_of_baby", "apgar_1", "apgar_5", "baby_nicu",
  # Laboratorio
  "platelet_count_delivery", "ast_delivery", "alt_delivery", "creatinine_delivery"
)


# 3. BUCLE DE ANÁLISIS AUTOMATIZADO
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Este bucle recorrerá cada variable, determinará su tipo, aplicará el test correcto
# e imprimirá el resultado.

# Creamos una lista para guardar los resultados significativos
resultados_significativos <- list()

for (variable in variables_clinicas_a_probar) {
  
  # Imprime un encabezado para cada variable para que la salida sea clara
  cat("\n--------------------------------------------------\n")
  cat("Analizando variable:", variable, "\n")
  cat("--------------------------------------------------\n")
  
  # --- Verificación de seguridad: ¿la columna existe? ---
  if (!variable %in% colnames(pe_subgroups_df)) {
    cat("   -> Advertencia: La variable '", variable, "' no se encontró en los datos. Omitiendo.\n")
    next # Salta a la siguiente variable en el bucle
  }
  
  # Crea la fórmula para los tests
  formula <- as.formula(paste0("`", variable, "` ~ PE_subgroup"))
  
  # --- Comprueba si la variable es numérica o un contador ---
  if (is.numeric(pe_subgroups_df[[variable]])) {
    
    # Realiza la prueba de Wilcoxon para variables numéricas
    test_resultado <- wilcox.test(formula, data = pe_subgroups_df)
    cat("Tipo: Numérica | Test: Wilcoxon rank-sum\n")
    cat("   -> p-valor:", format.pval(test_resultado$p.value, digits = 4), "\n")
    
    # Si el resultado es significativo, guárdalo
    if (test_resultado$p.value < 0.1) { # Usamos 0.1 como umbral exploratorio
      resultados_significativos[[variable]] <- test_resultado
    }
    
  } else { # --- Si no es numérica, la tratamos como categórica ---
    
    # Crea una tabla de contingencia
    tabla <- table(pe_subgroups_df[[variable]], pe_subgroups_df$PE_subgroup)
    
    # Comprobación de seguridad: Fisher necesita que la tabla tenga más de 1 fila y columna
    if (nrow(tabla) > 1 && ncol(tabla) > 1) {
      # Realiza la prueba Exacta de Fisher
      test_resultado <- fisher.test(tabla)
      cat("Tipo: Categórica | Test: Fisher's Exact\n")
      print(tabla)
      cat("   -> p-valor:", format.pval(test_resultado$p.value, digits = 4), "\n")
      
      # Si el resultado es significativo, guárdalo
      if (test_resultado$p.value < 0.1) {
        resultados_significativos[[variable]] <- test_resultado
      }
    } else {
      cat("   -> Omitiendo test para '", variable, "' (no hay variación en uno de los grupos).\n")
      print(tabla)
    }
  }
}

# 4. REVISAR RESULTADOS SIGNIFICATIVOS
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n##################################################\n")
cat("### RESUMEN DE RESULTADOS SIGNIFICATIVOS (p < 0.1) ###\n")
cat("##################################################\n")

if (length(resultados_significativos) > 0) {
  print(resultados_significativos)
} else {
  cat("No se encontraron diferencias significativas con un umbral de p < 0.1\n")
}
```

# SCRIPT PARA ANÁLISIS DE SUBGRUPOS DE PE ESTRATIFICADO POR ETNICIDAD

```{r}
# SCRIPT PARA ANÁLISIS DE SUBGRUPOS DE PE ESTRATIFICADO POR ETNICIDAD

# 1. SETUP Y PREPARACIÓN DE DATOS (Pasos iniciales como antes)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
library(phyloseq)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Asumimos que 'phy' y 'analysis_df' ya existen en tu entorno.
# Si no, créalos con el código de los scripts anteriores.
# analysis_df debe contener: study_id, log10_PB_ratio, study_group, y todas las variables clínicas.


# 2. DEFINIR LOS GRUPOS ÉTNICOS Y FILTRAR DATOS
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Creamos una nueva columna para nuestros grupos de interés
# y filtramos para quedarnos solo con las muestras de esos grupos.
analysis_stratified_df <- analysis_df %>%
  mutate(ethnic_group = case_when(
    ethnicity == "Hispanic/Latina" ~ "Hispanic",
    race == "White/Caucasian" & ethnicity == "Not Hispanic/Latina" ~ "White",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ethnic_group), study_group == "PE") # Nos enfocamos solo en pacientes con PE

# 3. IDENTIFICAR LOS SUBGRUPOS "HIGH-RATIO" DENTRO DE CADA GRUPO ÉTNICO
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# En lugar de un umbral fijo, definiremos el grupo "High-Ratio" como
# el ~25% superior de pacientes dentro de cada grupo étnico. Esto es más robusto.
# Puedes ajustar el porcentaje (quantile_threshold) si lo deseas.

quantile_threshold <- 0.75 # (1.0 - 0.75 = 0.25, o sea el 25% superior)

pe_ethnic_subgroups_df <- analysis_stratified_df %>%
  group_by(ethnic_group) %>% # Importante: agrupar por etnicidad
  mutate(PE_subgroup = case_when(
    log10_PB_ratio >= quantile(log10_PB_ratio, quantile_threshold, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "PE_High_Ratio",
    TRUE ~ "PE_Normal_Ratio"
  )) %>%
  ungroup() # Desagrupar para análisis posteriores

# Visualicemos los subgrupos que hemos creado
ggplot(pe_ethnic_subgroups_df, aes(x = ethnic_group, y = log10_PB_ratio, color = PE_subgroup)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Subgrupos de Ratio P/B definidos dentro de cada Grupo Étnico")


# 4. BUCLE DE ANÁLISIS CLÍNICO AUTOMATIZADO Y ESTRATIFICADO
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Definimos las variables a probar
variables_clinicas_a_probar <- c(
  "age", "bmi", "gravid", "par", "pre_weight", "gwg", "gestational_age",
  "baby_weight", "apgar_1", "apgar_5"
  # Puedes añadir más variables numéricas aquí
)

# Bucle principal que itera sobre cada variable clínica
for (variable in variables_clinicas_a_probar) {
  
  cat("\n========================================================\n")
  cat("### Analizando Variable Clínica:", variable, "###\n")
  cat("========================================================\n")
  
  # --- ANÁLISIS PARA EL GRUPO HISPANIC ---
  cat("\n--- Grupo: Hispanic ---\n")
  
  # Filtramos los datos solo para este grupo
  df_hispanic <- pe_ethnic_subgroups_df %>% filter(ethnic_group == "Hispanic")
  
  # Comprobamos si hay suficientes datos para comparar
  if (n_distinct(df_hispanic$PE_subgroup) == 2) {
    # Realizamos la prueba de Wilcoxon
    test_hisp <- wilcox.test(as.formula(paste0("`", variable, "` ~ PE_subgroup")), data = df_hispanic)
    cat("   -> p-valor (Wilcoxon):", format.pval(test_hisp$p.value, digits = 4), "\n")
  } else {
    cat("   -> No hay suficientes subgrupos para comparar.\n")
  }
  
  # --- ANÁLISIS PARA EL GRUPO WHITE ---
  cat("\n--- Grupo: White ---\n")
  
  # Filtramos los datos solo para este grupo
  df_white <- pe_ethnic_subgroups_df %>% filter(ethnic_group == "White")
  
  # Comprobamos si hay suficientes datos para comparar
  if (n_distinct(df_white$PE_subgroup) == 2) {
    # Realizamos la prueba de Wilcoxon
    test_white <- wilcox.test(as.formula(paste0("`", variable, "` ~ PE_subgroup")), data = df_white)
    cat("   -> p-valor (Wilcoxon):", format.pval(test_white$p.value, digits = 4), "\n")
  } else {
    cat("   -> No hay suficientes subgrupos para comparar.\n")
  }
}

```

```{r}
#lm of pregnant_woman_fecal_calpro_mg_kg by study_group ajusting by ELISA_run
# Load necessary libraries
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest) # To get p-values for mixed models
library(emmeans)  # For post-hoc analysis
phy <- readRDS("/Users/danielavargasrobles/Dropbox (UMass Medical School)/Ana_projects/2_PREECLAMPSIA/WGS/obj/phy_mtph_gtdb.rds")

#extract metadta
met <- as(sample_data(phy), "data.frame")
# Assume 'met' dataframe is already loaded

# 1. Check distribution of the dependent variable
hist(met$pregnant_woman_fecal_calpro_mg_kg, 
     main = "Distribution of Calprotectin", 
     xlab = "Calprotectin (mg/kg)")

# It's likely right-skewed. Let's create a log-transformed version.
# We use log1p() which calculates log(x + 1) to handle potential zeros.
met$log_calpro <- log1p(met$pregnant_woman_fecal_calpro_mg_kg)

hist(met$log_calpro, 
     main = "Distribution of Log-Transformed Calprotectin",
     xlab = "log(Calprotectin + 1)")

# Ensure ELISA_run is a factor
met$ELISA_run <- as.factor(met$ELISA_run)
met$study_group <- as.factor(met$study_group)

# 2. Build the Linear Model
# We model log_calpro as a function of study_group, adjusting for ELISA_run
fit_lm <- lm(log_calpro ~ study_group + ELISA_run, data = met)

# 3. Check the model summary
summary(fit_lm)

# To get a clean ANOVA table which is often easier to interpret:
anova(fit_lm)
```

```{r}
}


# --- Analysis for White/Caucasian (Not Hispanic/Latina) Group ---

cat("\n\n====================================================\n")
cat("ANALYSIS FOR: White/Caucasian (Not Hispanic/Latina) Group\n")
cat("====================================================\n\n")

# 2.a. Create a subset for the White/Caucasian group
met_white <- met_pe %>%
  filter(race == "White/Caucasian" & ethnicity == "Not Hispanic/Latina")

# 2.b. CRITICAL STEP: Check sample size in this stratum
cat("Sample counts for 'severe' in White/Caucasian group:\n")
print(table(met_white$severe))
cat(paste("Total samples in this group:", nrow(met_white), "\n\n"))

# Only proceed if you have enough samples
if (all(table(met_white$severe) > 5) && nrow(met_white) > 15) {
  # 2.c. Build and run the LMM for the White/Caucasian group
  fit_lmm_white <- lmer(log_calpro ~ severe + (1 | ELISA_run), data = met_white)
  
  cat("Model Summary (White/Caucasian):\n")
  print(summary(fit_lmm_white))
  
  cat("\nANOVA Table (White/Caucasian):\n")
  print(anova(fit_lmm_white))
} else {
  cat("Warning: Not enough samples to run a reliable model for the White/Caucasian group.\n")
}
```
#comparacion white vs Hispnic
```{r}
# Load necessary libraries if not already loaded
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(ggplot2)

# We use the original 'met' dataframe with all subjects
phy <- readRDS("/Users/danielavargasrobles/Dropbox (UMass Medical School)/Ana_projects/2_PREECLAMPSIA/WGS/obj/phy_mtph_gtdb.rds")

#extract metadta
met <- as(sample_data(phy), "data.frame")
# 1. Prepare the data for comparison
# Create a new dataframe containing only the two groups of interest
# And create a single, clean 'ethnicity_group' factor
met_ethnic_comparison <- met %>%
  mutate(ethnicity_group = case_when(
    ethnicity == "Hispanic/Latina" ~ "Hispanic/Latina",
    race == "White/Caucasian" & ethnicity == "Not Hispanic/Latina" ~ "White/Caucasian",
    TRUE ~ "Other" # Categorize all others as 'Other'
  )) %>%
  filter(ethnicity_group %in% c("Hispanic/Latina", "White/Caucasian")) %>%
  mutate(ethnicity_group = factor(ethnicity_group)) # Re-factor to drop unused levels

# Check the final counts
cat("Sample counts for the comparison:\n")
print(table(met_ethnic_comparison$ethnicity_group, met_ethnic_comparison$study_group))


# 2. Build the Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM)
# We model log_calpro as a function of ethnicity_group, 
# adjusting for study_group and controlling for ELISA_run.
fit_lmm_ethnic <- lmer(log_calpro ~ ethnicity_group + study_group + (1 | ELISA_run), 
                       data = met_ethnic_comparison)

cat("\n\n--- Model Results ---\n")
# Get the ANOVA-like table for the fixed effects
print(anova(fit_lmm_ethnic))

# For more detail on the direction of the effect
print(summary(fit_lmm_ethnic))


# 3. Visualize the results
# A boxplot is great for visualization. Faceting by study_group is helpful.
ggplot(met_ethnic_comparison, aes(x = ethnicity_group, y = log_calpro, fill = ethnicity_group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~study_group) + # <-- Separate plots for Control and PE
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Hispanic/Latina" = "#ef8a62", "White/Caucasian" = "#67a9cf")) +
  labs(
    title = "Calprotectin Levels by Ethnicity, Stratified by Study Group",
    x = "Ethnicity Group",
    y = "log(Calprotectin + 1)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
```
#Summary table
```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(rstatix) # For easy Wilcoxon tests

# --- 1. Data Preparation ---
# Same data preparation as before
met_clean <- met %>%
  rename(calprotectin = pregnant_woman_fecal_calpro_mg_kg) %>%
  mutate(ethnicity_group = case_when(
    ethnicity == "Hispanic/Latina" ~ "Hispanic",
    race == "White/Caucasian" & ethnicity == "Not Hispanic/Latina" ~ "White",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )) %>%
  filter(ethnicity_group %in% c("Hispanic", "White")) %>%
  mutate(
    study_group = factor(study_group, levels = c("Control", "PE")),
    severe = factor(severe, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
  )

# --- 2. Generate Table 1: Preeclampsia Status ---

# Create an empty list to store results for each row
results_list_status <- list()

# -- Row 1: All Individuals --
data_subset <- met_clean
desc_stats <- data_subset %>% group_by(study_group) %>% summarise(med = median(calprotectin, na.rm=T), mn = mean(calprotectin, na.rm=T))
p_val <- data_subset %>% wilcox_test(calprotectin ~ study_group) %>% pull(p)
results_list_status[['All']] <- tibble(
  Group = "All individuals",
  Control = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[1],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[1],1), ")"),
  PE = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[2],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[2],1), ")"),
  `P value` = round(p_val, 3)
)

# -- Row 2: Hispanic --
data_subset <- met_clean %>% filter(ethnicity_group == "Hispanic")
desc_stats <- data_subset %>% group_by(study_group) %>% summarise(med = median(calprotectin, na.rm=T), mn = mean(calprotectin, na.rm=T))
p_val <- data_subset %>% wilcox_test(calprotectin ~ study_group) %>% pull(p)
results_list_status[['Hispanic']] <- tibble(
  Group = "Hispanic",
  Control = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[1],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[1],1), ")"),
  PE = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[2],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[2],1), ")"),
  `P value` = round(p_val, 3)
)

# -- Row 3: White --
data_subset <- met_clean %>% filter(ethnicity_group == "White")
desc_stats <- data_subset %>% group_by(study_group) %>% summarise(med = median(calprotectin, na.rm=T), mn = mean(calprotectin, na.rm=T))
p_val <- data_subset %>% wilcox_test(calprotectin ~ study_group) %>% pull(p)
results_list_status[['White']] <- tibble(
  Group = "White",
  Control = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[1],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[1],1), ")"),
  PE = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[2],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[2],1), ")"),
  `P value` = round(p_val, 3)
)

# Combine all rows into a single table
table1_status <- bind_rows(results_list_status)


# --- 3. Generate Table 2: Preeclampsia Severe Features ---

met_pe_only <- met_clean %>% filter(study_group == "PE")
results_list_severe <- list()

# -- Row 1: All Individuals (PE only) --
data_subset <- met_pe_only
desc_stats <- data_subset %>% group_by(severe) %>% summarise(med = median(calprotectin, na.rm=T), mn = mean(calprotectin, na.rm=T))
p_val <- data_subset %>% wilcox_test(calprotectin ~ severe) %>% pull(p)
results_list_severe[['All']] <- tibble(
  Group = "All individuals",
  Without = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[1],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[1],1), ")"),
  With = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[2],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[2],1), ")"),
  `P value` = round(p_val, 3)
)

# -- Row 2: Hispanic (PE only) --
data_subset <- met_pe_only %>% filter(ethnicity_group == "Hispanic")
desc_stats <- data_subset %>% group_by(severe) %>% summarise(med = median(calprotectin, na.rm=T), mn = mean(calprotectin, na.rm=T))
p_val <- data_subset %>% wilcox_test(calprotectin ~ severe) %>% pull(p)
results_list_severe[['Hispanic']] <- tibble(
  Group = "Hispanic",
  Without = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[1],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[1],1), ")"),
  With = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[2],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[2],1), ")"),
  `P value` = round(p_val, 3)
)

# -- Row 3: White (PE only) --
data_subset <- met_pe_only %>% filter(ethnicity_group == "White")
desc_stats <- data_subset %>% group_by(severe) %>% summarise(med = median(calprotectin, na.rm=T), mn = mean(calprotectin, na.rm=T))
p_val <- data_subset %>% wilcox_test(calprotectin ~ severe) %>% pull(p)
results_list_severe[['White']] <- tibble(
  Group = "White",
  Without = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[1],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[1],1), ")"),
  With = paste0(round(desc_stats$med[2],1), " (", round(desc_stats$mn[2],1), ")"),
  `P value` = round(p_val, 3)
)

# Combine all rows into a single table
table2_severity <- bind_rows(results_list_severe)


# --- 4. Display Final Tables ---
cat("====================================================================\n")
cat("      Tabla: Comparación de Calprotectina por Estado de Preeclampsia\n")
cat("====================================================================\n")
print(table1_status, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n\n")
cat("====================================================================\n")
cat("      Tabla: Comparación de Calprotectina por Severidad (solo en PE)\n")
cat("====================================================================\n")
print(table2_severity, row.names = FALSE)
```
